sourceText: If you believe your bill is wrong, call us at 555-0100 or write to us within 30 days of the bill date. While we review your dispute, you need to pay only the part of the bill you do not dispute, and your service will not be disconnected for the amount in dispute.
Budget billing spreads your yearly electricity costs into equal monthly payments, so your bill is the same each month. We review your payment every six months and adjust it if your use has changed.

We never disconnect service for nonpayment without notice. We mail a written notice at least 10 days before the date service may be disconnected, and we call the phone on the account at least 2 days before that date.
A bill that is not paid in full by its due date is charged a late payment charge of 1.5 percent of the unpaid balance. The charge is applied once for each bill.
Our customer office at 100 Main Street is open Monday through Friday, from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., and is closed on weekends and public holidays. Outages can be reported by phone at any time, day or night.
Residential customers whose power is out for 24 hours or more in a row receive a credit of 25 dollars. The credit is applied automatically to the next bill. There is nothing to apply for.
The outage map at www.example.com/outages shows current outages, the number of customers affected, and the estimated time power will be restored. It is updated every 15 minutes.
You can pay online at www.example.com/pay, by automatic payment from a bank account, by phone at 555-0100, by mail, or in person at our customer office. There is no fee for any of these ways to pay.

Once the past-due amount is paid, or a payment arrangement is set up, service is reconnected within 24 hours. A reconnection fee of 30 dollars is added to the next bill. The fee is waived the first time in any 12 months.
The monthly bill is a customer charge of 12 dollars, plus an energy charge of 14.2 cents for each kilowatt-hour used in the billing period.

For the 2026 to 2027 heating season, effective October 1, 2026, households with income at or below 200 percent of the federal poverty guidelines can receive a one-time bill credit of up to 300 dollars. Applications are accepted from October 1, 2026 through March 31, 2027.

To start or stop service, apply online at www.example.com/start or call 555-0100 at least 3 business days before your move-in or move-out date. When you stop service, your final bill is mailed to your new address within 10 days.
